comments.author: TacticalCoder
comments.why_zh: 带音乐的 256 字节 C64 demo
comments.text_zh: 到现在，我一看到“linusakesson.net”就会不看内容先点赞，然后读 TFA、看视频（这次是听音乐）。我从来没失望过。说到这个，我打算做一件真的很酷的事：我有一台“时间胶囊”C64（其实是 C128，但差不多），而且它还能用。它从没被任何现代东西“污染”过：没有“gotek”SD 读卡器，什么都没有：就是一台来自八十年代早期到中期的真正时间胶囊。我打算手动编码 linusakesson 的“A mind is born”C64 demo 的那 256 个字节（没错，就是字节）。然后运行它（当然是把 C128 接到旧 CRT 上），想着从技术上讲，我本来在八十年代就能编码并运行它。真是令人脑洞大开：[VIDEO]
comments.text: By now when I see "linusakesson.net" I upvote without reading, then I read TFA and watch the vid (or listen to the music in this case). I'm never disappointed. Speaking of which I plan to do something really cool: I've got a "time capsule" C64 (well C128 but close enough) and it still works. It's never been "polluted" by anything modern: no "gotek" SD reader, no nothing: just a real time capsule from the early to mid eighties. And I plan to encode, manually, the 256 bytes (yes, bytes) of linusakesson's "A mind is born" C64 demo. I'll then run it (with the C128 hooked to an old CRT, of course), thinking that technically I could have encoded and ran that in the eighties. Mind blowing stuff: [VIDEO]

comments.author: yetihehe
comments.story_title: Mathematical Simplicity May Drive Evolution's Speed
comments.why_zh: 看似丰富的结构其实来自被微调的随机数据
comments.quote_zh: 它只是被微调/挑选过的随机数据
comments.text_zh: > DNA 极其重要，但如果它不处在细胞、生物体、生态系统中，就毫无意义。还有其他相互作用在起作用，而算法信息论的这种应用无法捕捉到那种复杂性的全貌。这让我想到 demoscene，特别是 "A mind is born"[1]，那个 256 字节的 demo，它“看起来”很复杂、结构丰富，但其实只是被微调/挑选过的随机数据。作者说，他当初就是拿一些随机生成的内容反复试，直到找到满意的结果。单是这 256 字节本身，仍然不足以复制行为，它必须运行在硬件上，而硬件就像是 DNA 的“环境”。如果没有几个容易访问的辅助芯片，那段代码毫无意义，也产生不了那样的复杂性。更何况，demo 里的那些“图案”之所以是图案，只是因为“我们”把它们解读为有意义的。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: > DNA is extremely important, but it makes no sense if [it is] not in a cell, in an organism, in an ecosystem. Other interactions are at play, and this application of algorithmic information cannot capture the extent of that complexity. It reminds me of demoscene, specifically "A mind is born"[1], 256-byte demo which "looks" complicated and with rich structure, but it's just nudged/selected random data. Author said that he played around with some random generated content until he found something nice. Just by itself that 256 bytes is still not enough to replicate behaviour, it must be run on hardware, which is like "environment" for DNA. Without several supporting chips which are easy to access, that code would mean nothing and would not generate such complexity. Moreover, those "patterns" in demo are patterns only because WE interpret them as meaningful. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: verytrivial
comments.story_title: Dialog – domain-specific language for interactive fiction
comments.why_zh: Linus Akesson 在 C64 上的工作
comments.quote_zh: 在我眼里，Linus 有着极其硬核的编程资历！
comments.text_zh: 不知为何，我对这些 IF 引擎很着迷。在我看来，Dialog 的特别之处在于它与同一作者开发的 Å-machine 虚拟机结合后，在 6502 上取得的性能。它是一门领域特定语言 + 优化编译器 + 运行时，面向的是一个已经几十年没有新产的平台（C64）。C64 上有一些很出色的 Z-machine 实现，但基本上任何使用 Inform7 运行时（一堆便利的解析和世界技巧）的东西都跑得像条狗。Dialog + Å-machine 绕过了中间层，达到了相当可观且不断提升的水平。在我眼里，Linus 有着极其硬核的编程资历！[LINK] [VIDEO]
comments.text: I am fascinated by these IF engines for some reason. What sets the Dialog apart is, IMHO, the performance it gets on 6502 in combination with the Å-machine VM by the same author. It's a domain specific language + optimized compiler + runtime for a platform (C64) that hasn't been made for decades. There are some excellent Z-machine impls for C64, but basically anything using the Inform7 runtime (a bunch of convenience parsing and world tricks) runs like a dog. Dialog + Å-machines gets a respectable and growing amount of the way there but cutting out the middle man. Linus has some extreme coding cred in my book! [LINK] [VIDEO]

comments.author: pflanze
comments.story_title: Infinite Mac: An Instant-Booting Quadra in the Browser
comments.text_zh:
> 而且它极其复杂，做的远不止这些。

谁说得准呢？这个讨论中有趣的一点是代码规模为什么这么大，而详细看看程序到底做了什么会是一个起点。当然，可以设想使用高级语言会让写代码更容易，因此会写出更多代码。或者，只要愿意装作知道，你或我其实可以得出任何我们想要的结论。知道这一点会很有意思，但那需要花功夫去弄清楚。而我是个懒鬼。

PS：不想再争了 :)，但我现在已经查过 rsync 3.2.3 的大小，它是 51 Kloc 的 C 代码（包括所附 zlib 副本的 6300 loc）。在不比较功能的情况下，你还需要加上一个加密库、一个 GUI 库以及 GUI 代码，才能让它成为 Dropbox 的可行替代品。Git annex 8.20210223 是 70 Kloc 的 Haskell 和 9100 loc 的 JavaScript，但它依赖 Git 来完成工作，而 Git（版本 2.30.2）是 327 Kloc 的 C 代码和 225 Kloc 的 sh 与 Perl 代码。Thunar 4.16.8 是 73 Kloc 的 C 代码，sshfs 是 4700 loc，fuse 是 22 Kloc 的 C，openssh 是 113 Kloc 的 C，所以也许你可以用 212 Kloc 的 C 构建一个 Dropbox 替代品，而无需审视功能集。也许那仍然比 Dropbox 客户端小 4-5 倍，但你说的 50 Kloc 这个数字又差了 4 倍。 :)

（我猜有人会说，真值“介于两者之间”，如果在对数尺度上看这些数字的话……）我相信你也能想出一个小得多的
comments.text: > and it is extremely complex and does much more Who's to say? The interesting bit in this discussion is why the code size is large, and looking in detail what the programs do would be a start. Of course, one could suppose that using a high-level language makes it easier to write code, hence, more code is going to be written. Or you or I could really conclude anything we want, if we're willing to pretend to know. It would be interesting to know, but that takes work to find out. And I'm a lazy bastard. PS. not to argue any more :), but I have checked the size of rsync 3.2.3 now, it's 51 Kloc of C code (including the 6300 loc of the included copy of zlib). You'd need to add a cryptographic library, a GUI library, and GUI code to make it a viable replacement for Dropbox, without comparing features. Git annex 8.20210223 is 70 Kloc of Haskell and 9100 loc of JavaScript, but it depends on Git to do its work, which (version 2.30.2) is 327 Kloc of C code and 225 Kloc of sh and Perl code. Thunar 4.16.8 is 73 Kloc of C code, sshfs is 4700 loc and fuse is 22 Kloc of C, openssh is 113 Kloc of C, so maybe you could build a Dropbox replacement in 212 Kloc of C without looking through the feature set. Maybe that's still 4-5 times smaller than the Dropbox client, but your number of 50 Kloc is again off by a factor of 4. :) (I guess one could say that the truth is "somewhere in the middle", looking at those number on a logarithmic scale...) I'm sure you could also come up with a much smaller
